tasks.title: Workspace-write vendored default + hooks.json joins the frozen vendor surface
tasks.objective: Close the dormant full-access default: the vendored .codex/config.toml flips sandbox_mode to workspace-write with an escape-hatch comment pointing at decision 0041, and check_vendor_integrity.py adds .codex/hooks.json to the hashed vendor surface so a client edit disarming a vendored hook fails the frozen-gate audit. Manifest tests prove drift detection and re-vendor repair; a config-default assertion joins the init/upgrade hook tests.
acceptance_criteria: In .codex/config.toml, sandbox_mode changes from danger-full-access to workspace-write (currently ~line 15). Add a short comment above it: broader access requires deliberately editing this value in the client repo — the diff-visible edit is the ledgered escape hatch per docs/decisions/0041-sandboxed-workers-default.md, and forge upgrade restores this default. Nothing else in the file changes.

factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py adds .codex/hooks.json to the hashed vendor surface list (currently factory/scripts, factory/schemas, factory/prompts, forge, .claude/settings.json — see ~line 23). Manifest generation (write_manifest in scaffold/adopt/upgrade) derives from the shared surface definition, so verify whether the list is shared or duplicated; if duplicated, update every copy so init, adopt, upgrade, and the checker agree — a checker that hashes what the writer never manifests would fail every clean client.

factory/tests/test_gates.py: extend test_scaffold_freezes_gate_surface_and_check_verifies (~:12377) to assert the generated manifest covers .codex/hooks.json and that editing hooks.json in the scaffolded client fails check_vendor_integrity with the drift named; extend test_adopt_and_upgrade_refreeze_the_manifest (~:12615) to prove adopt/upgrade repair a drifted hooks.json and re-hash it clean. Add an assertion near test_init_and_upgrade_ship_portable_hook_commands (~:2572) that the vendored config.toml carries sandbox_mode = "workspace-write" after init and after upgrade.

Full gate suite green (uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q) — content pins for the vendor surface live in differently-named tests, so the FULL suite is the proof, not a -k slice.
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "manifest or freeze or portable_hook"
tasks.reviewer_focus: The surface-list agreement is the trap: if the hashed list is defined in more than one place, all writers and the checker must agree or every clean client fails integrity. The config comment must not promise enforcement the mechanism lacks (visibility, not prevention). The flip must not touch delegation argv or any other config key.

plan_contracts.statement: The vendored .codex/config.toml defaults sandbox_mode to workspace-write with a comment documenting the deliberate-edit escape hatch and pointing at decision 0041; forge upgrade restores the default.
check_vendor_integrity hashes .codex/hooks.json, every manifest writer agrees, and tests prove both drift detection and re-vendor repair.
config.toml is deliberately not hashed, and decision 0041 records the flip, the escape-hatch doctrine, and the honest statement that delegation already ran workspace-write.
A real delegation passes end to end under the companion's workspace-write mapping, recorded in the testing artifact.
